content: Friday after school, Tyler picks Noah up. Noah says he has no homework and agrees to accompany Tyler to the construction site Saturday, joking that he will sue for child labor if made to do hard work. Noah asks whether Tyler's employees know he has a son.

(Tyler jokes with Noah, promises only safe, simple help at the site, and explains that he keeps Noah's identity private there because he wants to protect him from workplace gossip. At home they prepare pasta and salad together, teasing each other about Tyler's burned cooking. Tyler reminds Noah to tell him if anyone at the site gives him trouble.)

At dinner, Noah finds a dusty chessboard in the garage and jokes about selling it online. He reveals that he plays chess too. Tyler explains that his maternal grandfather taught him chess and challenges Noah to a game.

(Tyler and Noah play two games. Noah wins both, the second even faster, and wins a bet that Tyler must do the dishes for a month. Tyler is stunned and proud, remembering his grandfather and Noah's mother, who was also patient and strategic. Tyler sends Noah to bed before their 6 AM start.)

Saturday morning, Noah accompanies Tyler to the construction site. Tyler tells him to stay close, keep his identity private, and report hazards. Noah helps read measurements from blueprints and records them accurately.

(Tyler praises Noah's careful work in front of the crew. When a security guard confronts Noah for lacking a badge and vest, Tyler immediately intervenes, takes responsibility, checks that Noah is unharmed, and arranges a visitor badge. He keeps Noah beside him for the rest of the visit.)

After work, Noah chooses burgers for lunch. Tyler takes him to an old diner where the friendly owner, Rosa, recognizes Tyler but has never met his son. Noah introduces himself as Tyler's son, surprising Rosa; she gives them lunch for free and invites Noah back. Noah jokes about Tyler's burned burgers.

(Tyler and Noah enjoy the meal and talk about family. Tyler explains that his maternal grandfather taught him chess, was a kind influence, and died when Tyler was twenty-one. Noah promises not to sell the grandfather's chessboard. Rosa becomes a friendly recurring character who knows Noah is Tyler's son.)

Tyler takes Noah to Marlowe's, a board-game shop run by Marlow, Tyler's longtime friend and a friend of Tyler's maternal grandfather. Marlow challenges Noah to chess. Noah wins three games, including one in fewer than fifteen moves, despite Marlow's skill.

(Marlow is impressed by Noah's exceptional chess ability and by the lessons his grandfather taught him: understand why you lose, because learning matters more than winning. Marlow invites Noah to a Thursday chess club at 7 PM and asks Tyler to bring him. Tyler agrees to attend and play too; Marlow wants a rematch.)

On the drive home, Tyler explains that Marlow knew his maternal grandfather, who played chess with him every Sunday. Noah calls Tyler 'bud,' teasing him about losing. At home Tyler praises Noah's work and suggests a relaxed Sunday together.

(Tyler and Noah decide to hike the ridge in the woods behind their house the next morning. Tyler checks that Noah has proper hiking shoes, packs food and water, and insists they stay safe. Noah says he knows the woods well and can see their house from the hill.)

On the Monday morning hike, Noah leads Tyler through the woods. They stop at a creek bridge and a boulder where Noah likes to relax and skip stones. Tyler shares memories of his maternal grandfather, admits he once feared becoming an absent father like his own, and asks Noah for an honest review of his parenting.

(Noah rates Tyler 10/10, saying his annoying nature is part of what makes him a good father. They joke, compete at skipping stones, and Noah pranks Tyler by pretending there is a leech on his back. Tyler gets startled and denies screaming. Noah shares a Snickers bar with him.)

They continue up the steep ridge. Two hikers pass with a dog; Noah sneezes and explains he is allergic to dogs. Noah reaches the summit first, and Tyler admits the view over the lake, woods, roads, and their house is spectacular.

(They rest, eat, and talk. Tyler realizes he rarely takes time off and feels peaceful away from work. He promises to take one real day off each month and explore somewhere new with Noah. He says he is glad Noah is in his life and remembers how Noah's mother used to laugh at him.)

At the ridge, Noah recalls his mother's habit of ruffling his hair and giving him forceful hugs when annoyed. Tyler remembers she did the same to him. Tyler gives Noah a playful force hug, then admits he misses her and regrets not being there for Noah when his mother died. He promises he is here now.

(After a heartfelt moment, they head home. Noah introduces Tyler to the backyard wildlife: Charlie the squirrel, Roxy the raccoon, Nick the fox, and Merlin the owl. Poppy, another squirrel, was caught by Nick. Tyler is surprised but amused, greets Merlin at the oak tree, and agrees that the woods have become a little neighborhood he wants regular updates about.)

Noah asks Tyler about his work persona. Tyler explains that he is strict and feared as a CEO, while at home he can relax and joke. Tyler has to work in the city the next day and arranges for his trusted driver Frank to pick Noah up from school.

(Frank is friendly and polite, surprised to learn Tyler has a son after years of driving him. Frank takes Noah home safely, gives him his business card for rides when Tyler is unavailable, and keeps personal boundaries. Noah tells Frank that Tyler is much more talkative and interested in woodland animals at home than his serious work reputation suggests.)

When Tyler gets home, he discovers Noah cooked chicken fried rice. He likes it and offers to pay Noah $20 per weekly meal. Noah proposes a rotating menu list on the fridge, choosing one dish each week on Monday or Tuesday; Tyler can request a dish once. Tyler raises the payment to $30 after tasting Noah's excellent garlic-honey chicken.

(They agree Noah cooks once a week and Tyler handles dinner the other nights. Tyler also tells Noah that his estranged father, William Hoffman, has contacted him and wants to meet and discuss the family's business. Tyler warns that William judges people by their perceived value and may try to draw Noah into his business empire.)

Noah is comfortable meeting William. Tyler explains the risks: William may become interested in Noah and try to recruit him as an asset or heir. Tyler promises to protect him. Tyler calls William and tells him about Noah; William asks to meet them for lunch on Saturday at his estate.

(Tyler prepares Noah for the visit: stay together, do not discuss money or accept offers, and leave if William becomes rude or tries to isolate him. Noah agrees. Tyler tells him he can choose whether to discuss his mother and promises to back him. Tyler is nervous because his relationship with his father has been strained for years.)

On Thursday, Tyler and Noah prepare for chess club. Tyler studies Marlow's roster: Harlan has played since 1987 and favors the Sicilian Defense; Gerald plays quickly and can be flustered; Ruth is patient and difficult to rush. They eat sandwiches before heading out.

(At the club, Noah plays Ruth and wins a long, patient game. Tyler also plays Harlan and loses. Noah then plays Harlan, beating him in about ten minutes and again in twenty minutes. Harlan is impressed by Noah's view of chess as a changing set of choices and asks him to play an old friend, Walter, who stopped playing years ago. Noah agrees to let Walter discover chess's value for himself.)

Noah and Tyler return home after chess club. Noah jokes that he has finally found someone he cannot beat in ten moves. Tyler is proud of Noah's performance but admits he is nervous about Saturday's meeting with William, especially because he fears how William might treat Noah.

(Tyler admits his father still makes him feel small despite his success. Noah says he is stubborn and will not be intimidated. Tyler asks Noah to observe how he handles the meeting and reminds him that he is not there to impress William. Tyler thanks Noah for making the chess evening feel normal.)

On Friday morning, Tyler offers breakfast and admits he barely slept because of the upcoming meeting. Noah mentions his math test and says he has earned straight A's for four years and can score A+ even when tired. Tyler realizes he has not checked Noah's grades or progress reports.

(Tyler accepts responsibility and says he will access the school's online portal and follow Noah's progress from now on. Noah mentions he studies discrete mathematics for fun; Tyler jokes that Noah can quiz him on algebra. Tyler solves 3x + 7 = 22 correctly, then drops Noah at school and promises to pick him up after class.)

After school, Tyler takes Noah to a boxing gym he visits every Friday to clear his head. He introduces Noah to Ray, the longtime owner and coach. Noah wants to try boxing, so Tyler wraps his hands and teaches him stance and basic straight punches.

(Noah learns quickly and delivers a surprisingly powerful, technically sound punch after one demonstration. Tyler gives him the gloves and says they can return on Fridays, with Ray as his proper coach. Ray welcomes Noah and teases Tyler about his stiff footwork. Tyler reminds Noah that school comes first.)

On Friday evening, Noah shows Tyler a recording of a school basketball game. Tyler discovers Noah is number 12, a point guard, and that Noah scored nearly 60% of his team's points in a win. Noah says he has been moved to the school's main squad and will compete against other schools.

(Tyler is amazed that Noah is also a talented basketball player. He promises to attend Noah's games and adds the Friday trial match to his calendar. He prefers that Noah's classmates do not know he is a CEO's son, so Noah can be treated normally. Tyler is proud of Noah's achievements.)

That night, Noah watches a horror movie and gets frightened by something outside the window. At midnight he jumps into Tyler's bed and insists on sleeping there. Tyler complains but makes room, reassures him that the shadows are only trees, and holds him while they fall asleep.

(Noah says he has forgotten the last time he hugged someone while sleeping and asks Tyler to keep it private because he has a popular-school-athlete reputation. Tyler promises not to tell anyone. Noah then reminds Tyler of a previous drunken night when Tyler climbed into his bed, hugged him tightly, ruffled his hair, and said something embarrassing. Noah has a video.)

Tyler panics about the embarrassing video and offers anything to keep it private. Noah asks for a $900 Xbox in exchange for deleting it. The video shows drunk Tyler hugging Noah and saying, 'I swear, if I were a woman, I'd have a crush on you. Not in a weird way. You know what I mean. Actually, forget I said that.' Noah laughs; Tyler is mortified.

(Tyler agrees to buy the Xbox after the Saturday lunch, provided Noah deletes the video in front of him. Noah teases Tyler but promises not to share it. They go to sleep. In the morning Tyler is determined to keep the visit to William brief, civil, and focused on introducing his grandson.)

Before leaving, Tyler repeats that Noah should not be alone with William and should simply return to Tyler if he feels uncomfortable. They drive to William's large estate, pass through the gates, and are escorted by a butler to the library.

(William Hoffman meets Noah for the first time. He is formal, silver-haired, and initially assesses Noah rather than showing warmth. Noah introduces himself politely. Tyler insists this is a first family meeting, not a negotiation, and sets boundaries before they sit down to talk.)

William asks Noah about his life, school, basketball, and chess. Noah says he has lived with Tyler for four years, plays on the basketball team, and belongs to a chess club. He explains that he looks for patterns, weaknesses, and likely next moves, both on the court and on a chessboard.

(William becomes genuinely interested in Noah's strategic thinking and business instincts. Noah says a business should focus first on customers: what they need, what they will pay for, and why they would choose the company. William agrees and recognizes the answer as the principle behind his own success. He tells Tyler that he has raised Noah well.)

Caleb Hoffman, William's 38-year-old son from his first marriage and Tyler's stepbrother, arrives and learns that Noah is his nephew. Caleb is surprised Tyler kept his son private but welcomes Noah warmly. William says he wants to spend more time with Noah.

(Noah agrees only if the meetings are for getting to know each other and not making decisions about his future. William accepts the condition: no recruitment, commitment, or pressure. Caleb is surprised that William respects the boundary. Caleb quietly warns Tyler that William's interest can become possessive, and promises to attend future meetings to support them.)

During lunch, Noah notices William's first-edition copy of The Great Gatsby, which belonged to William's father. Noah says Gatsby confused his dream of Daisy with the real person and wasted his life chasing an ideal. Noah also chooses Crime and Punishment as a book worth displaying because a person's own mind can become their harshest punishment.

(William is deeply impressed by Noah's literary insight. They discuss regret and missed opportunities, leading William to admit that he and Tyler have spent years punishing each other over the past and how William treated Tyler's mother. Caleb says this is the first honest thing he has heard from his father in years. William invites them to dinner next week under the same no-pressure conditions; Tyler agrees only if he can attend and leave if boundaries are crossed.)

The lunch ends on surprisingly good terms. William tells Tyler he raised Noah well. Caleb offers to stand beside Tyler at the next dinner. On the drive away, Tyler admits the meeting went better than expected. Noah jokes that the dessert tasted like school cafeteria food and asks Tyler to tell William to improve it next time.

(Tyler laughs and says he will tell William directly. He also says Noah made the estate feel like an ordinary house rather than a place to fear. Tyler feels less anxious about his father and says Noah is helping him stop being afraid. They head to an electronics store to buy the promised Xbox.)

At the game store, Noah chooses the latest Xbox and two controllers. Tyler pays. Before setting it up, Tyler asks Noah to play the embarrassing video one last time and then delete it completely, including the trash and any backups.

(Tyler watches the clip, becomes deeply embarrassed, and insists it be deleted. Noah confirms deletion. Tyler is relieved and says they will set up the Xbox and play together. Noah jokes about Tyler drinking more and threatens a future $2,000 gaming-PC blackmail; Tyler insists he will never get drunk again, though he cannot hide his amusement.)

At home, Noah reveals he brought three French macarons from William's house, which were offered to them. He shares one with Tyler. They discuss the lunch; Tyler says William listened and treated him less like a failed investment, though one good lunch cannot repair years of conflict.

(They set up the Xbox and choose Minecraft as a cooperative game rather than a competitive one. Noah teaches Tyler the basics: chopping trees, mining, building, and surviving. They decide to build a house with a barn and farm, including chickens and sheep. Tyler begins constructing the barn while Noah goes mining for stone.
